01Why now

Why this course, and why now

Agents read untrusted text and then act: they send, spend, change records and run code. That makes the model the wrong place to rely on for safety. This course is built on one rule: the model may propose an action, but independently enforced policy decides whether that action is allowed to affect the world.

02Outcomes

What you will be able to do

Threat-model an agent

Map what an agent can read, remember, call and change, and where each attack can enter.

Enforce policy outside the model

Design identity, tool access, sandboxing and approvals so a manipulated model still cannot do harm.

Test it like an attacker

Plan and run authorised red-team tests against agents, and judge the results.

Detect, respond and govern

Monitor agents, contain an incident, recover, and keep the evidence an auditor or insurer will ask for.

04The lab

Design and assure a secure agentic system

Take one agent from a threat model to an assurance report: policy outside the model, contained execution, monitoring, and an authorised attack test. One project, built in steps after each lesson. Each step has instructions, a finished example, a health check, and saves on your device.

The steps

  1. Map the agent’s tools, data and authority
  2. Threat-model it and rank the risks
  3. Write the policy that decides which actions may run
  4. Contain code execution and credentials
  5. Add monitoring, alerts and a kill switch
  6. Run an authorised attack test and write the assurance report

What the health check looks for

  • Every tool has an owner and least privilege
  • The model cannot approve its own actions
  • Evidence shows each control is tested, monitored and recoverable
